theme: 3 terms on dark mode: the light or dark look, the color that adapts, and the screen facts a view can read

terms.definition: The light or dark look that the screen uses.
terms.example: Set the Interface Style to dark only for the video player.

terms.definition: A color that switches between its light and dark versions by itself.
terms.example: Use a Dynamic Color for the card, so it looks good at night.
terms.code:
let card = UIColor { traits in
    traits.userInterfaceStyle == .dark
        ? .black : .white
}

terms.definition: A set of facts about the screen, such as light or dark mode and size, that a view can read.
terms.example: Check the Trait Collection before you pick the image.

video.title: Interface Style, Dynamic Color & Trait Collection | Day 112
video.description:
Learn to explain how an iOS app supports dark mode: Interface Style, Dynamic Color & Trait Collection, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Interface Style - The light or dark look that the screen uses.
Dynamic Color - A color that switches between its light and dark versions by itself.
Trait Collection - A set of facts about the screen, such as light or dark mode and size, that a view can read.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

Explain Interface Style, Dynamic Color & Trait Collection in iOS by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.

Interface Style - The light or dark look that the screen uses.
한국어: 인터페이스 스타일: 화면이 쓰는 라이트 또는 다크 모양

Dynamic Color - A color that switches between its light and dark versions by itself.
한국어: 다이내믹 컬러: 라이트와 다크 버전을 스스로 바꾸는 색

Trait Collection - A set of facts about the screen, such as light or dark mode and size, that a view can read.
한국어: 트레이트 컬렉션: 다크 모드나 크기 같은 화면 정보를 모아 둔 집합

dialogue.title: Too bright at night

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, our card looks too bright at night.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Is the background a fixed white?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. I set it with a normal color.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use a Dynamic Color instead, like in the code.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How does it know the Interface Style?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The closure gets the Trait Collection and reads `userInterfaceStyle`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So the Trait Collection tells us dark or light.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. It also holds the screen size.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Can I force light mode on one screen?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Set the Interface Style on that view. But try not to.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I agree. The Dynamic Color handles it better.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly. Let the user choose their Interface Style.

dialogue.code:
let card = UIColor { traits in
    traits.userInterfaceStyle == .dark
        ? .black : .white
}
view.backgroundColor = card
